entry.title: Death Stranding 2 bridges the gap between PC and console
entry.summary:
Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, the long-awaited sequel to the first Strand-type game, is finally building a bridge between console and PC. Set to drop on March 19, Death Stranding 2 will let players complete the saga of Sam Bridges, a man caught up in a mysterious and strange world where the line between life and death has been erased.
This was announced during Sony's first 2026 State of Play, airing at the time of this article. Kojima Productions initially launched the game last summer as the final entry (so far) into the Death Stranding story. It picks up some time after the end of the first game and follows Sam Bridges as he travels across the Land Down Under, connecting Australia to the Chiral Network and establishing a link between it and what remains of the rest of the world.
Death Stranding 2 is one of the best stories ever told in video games, much like the first gamer was. Image via Sony
Death Stranding 2 is more cinematic and epic in scale, focusing on gameplay over cutscenes that had become Kojima's staple in prior games. Our Sr. Staff Writer, Scott Duwe, gave it a 9 out of 10, highlighting the game's incredible emotional impact, refined gameplay, and incredible graphical fidelity that set it apart from most games released in 2025, and certainly from PlayStation 5 titles.
It's one of the best games I have ever played, and while it's not as revolutionary or culturally impactful as the first one, it's still a sight to behold, refining Kojima's storytelling formula that should become the staple of video game narratives.
Death Stranding 2: On the Beach launches on PC on March 19 after a period of PS5 exclusivity that the first game adhered to as well.

entry.title: How to play Roadside Research with your friends
entry.summary:
Co-op title Roadside Research is now live on early access, and it's an adventure best shared with your buddies.
While there's a single-player mode that lets you enjoy the content alone, Roadside Research can be enjoyed in co-op up to four players. Whether you're playing via the Xbox Game Pass or using Steam, inviting your friends is a simple task.
Table of contents How to co-op in Roadside Research How many players can play together in Roadside Research
How to co-op in Roadside Research
For simplicity's sake, I will assume that you're hosting the game. Create a new save that you want to enjoy with your buddies. Single-player saves can't be used when playing with other players. Once you load into a co-op save, press the Escape button. You can now invite your friends.
Screenshot by Destructoid
If you're on Steam, you need to add your friends on the platform. The same rule applies to those playing via the Xbox Game Pass. If one of your friends is hosting a game, choose Join Friend. You'll get the option to join them on a shared session (assuming they're hosting a co-op save).
That's how easy it is to play co-op with your friends. Make sure that the person hosting the game stays online for the session to remain active.
How many players can play together in Roadside Research
Roadside Research can be enjoyed by up to four players in the same lobby. Of course, having four players is not necessary. For co-op, having a single buddy is enough. However, the more the merrier, I suppose.
While there's no matchmaking, you can use the official Discord to find other players looking to play together. Simply add them on Steam (or to your Xbox friends list) so that they can join your save.

entry.title: Well, it looks like Highguard is on life support – ‘This one really stings,’ says one laid-off dev
entry.summary:
As many probably expected, Highguard's development studio, Wildlight Entertainment, is seeing significant layoffs amid the game's less-than-stellar performance. One developer shared that "most of the team" has been let go, but the studio itself said only a "number" of non-essential developers were affected.
"Today we made an incredibly difficult decision to part ways with a number of our team members," the studio said on X. A "core group of developers" will remain at the company to "continue innovating on and supporting the game." This implies only non-essential workers were let go, perhaps even contractors, while the game is supposed to continue chugging along at the same or slightly lower pace.
This is a little different from what level designer Alex Graner said in a LinkedIn post preceding the official announcement by Wildlight. "Along with most of the team at Wildlight, I was laid off today," Graner wrote, saying this particular layoff "really stings" as the team has crafted tons of content that will probably never see the light of day (or, at least, won't be seen through to release by its creators).
From how Graner puts it, Wildlight Entertainment seems to have shed a lot more staff than what its post on X would have us believe. A "number" of non-core developers is in stark contrast to "most of the team." At any rate, a major restructuring has happened internally, and only time can tell how Highguard will turn out.
Recently, I tried to look at it from a more positive perspective. I thought maybe Wildlight would retreat into the shadows, performing its due diligence and perhaps turning the tide around, much like No Man's Sky did after falling from 200,000 to 1,000 players (that one is still getting major updates, by the way). However, it turns out I was dead wrong, or maybe this is a necessary move to ensure long-term plans are put into motion.
We'll see.

entry.title: How will co-op work in Subnautica 2
entry.summary:
Subnautica 2's latest trailer has given a glimpse of how co-op will work in the upcoming title, and you'll be able to share your experience with your buddy.
Unlike the two older titles, Subnautica 2 will have complete support for co-op. While you can survive the isolation on your own, you can also bring a friend with you.
Subnautica 2 co-op explained
Subnautica and Subnautica: Below Zero were single-player experiences. All decisions you made in the game were entirely dependent on your decision-making. Subnautica 2 will have the same features available for the players, but a co-op mode will also be available.
Co-op in Subnautica 2 won't be like how it works in It Takes Two or Split Fiction. It will be optional, but there's native support. All party members will be playing in the same shared world. However, the players will be free when it comes to making in-game decisions. They can engage in the same activity or decide to do something else.
In essence, you can convert your single-player worlds to multiplayer. Doing so will allow them to retain their progression for co-op. However, you can also create a new world to enjoy the game in co-op. Thanks to cross-platform support at launch, players using different systems will be able to play together.
There will be a few co-op exclusive features in Subnautica 2.
A two-seater Seaglider
The Dive Elevator will help to transport players and equipment from the deep depths, allowing you to save plenty of time (and maybe, your life if you're about to run out of oxygen)
While everything looks fantastic as of writing, we have yet to have confirmed information about the launch date. Subnautica 2 is expected to be out in early access later this year.

entry.title: How to get the Crimson Wolf weapon variant in Overwatch
entry.summary:
With each new season and update in Overwatch, loads of new content and cosmetics get added in, and this latest patch is no exception.
The Crimson Wolf weapon variant is the new seasonal crown jewel, though the UI doesn't exactly display how you can unlock it and for which currency. Thankfully, that's easily solved, so here's all you need to know.
Unlocking the Crimson Wolf weapon variant in Overwatch
The Crimson Wolf weapon variat is going to take you a good while to grind. Screenshot by Destructoid
This weapon variant requires you to spend 3,000 Competitive Points to unlock it, even if it doesn't display the exact currency cost in the UI itself. To earn Competitive Points, you have to play matches in the Competitive Mode or do Stadium Matches, only getting them if you win or draw.
You get 10 Competitive Points per Competitive win, five for draws, and 20 Competitive Points if you win in Stadium matches.
Additional points can be earned by progressing the Competitive and Stadium modes to earn 100 bonus Competitive Points per mode. You need to get 15 "Progress," with wins granting three and losses giving one point in that progression bar. Even with this bonus, you'll have to win a ton of games to be able to unlock the Crimson Wolf variant.
There are also the Legacy Competitive Points that carry over into the next season if you don't earn enough of them. They can then be spent on acquiring content from previous seasons and cannot be exchanged into actual Competitive Points. The Crimson Wolf weapon variant, at the moment, requires the regular stuff.
The post How to get the Crimson Wolf weapon variant in Overwatch appeared first on Destructoid.

entry.title: “You gotta let some of the chaos in”: Diablo 2's art lead explains what he doesn’t like about Diablo 4
entry.summary:
Last week, Moon Beast Productions officially revealed Darkhaven, a new action-RPG in the spirit of Diablo II, but with a changing, destructible, procedurally generated world that both echoes Minecraft and takes inspiration from the Diablo modding scene. Moon Beast are made up of ARPG royalty – their senior staff include original Diablo senior designer, art director and writer Erich Schaefer, Diablo 2 art lead Philip Shenk and Diablo 2 programmer Peter Hu.
As you’d expect, the Darkhaven devs have many Thoughts about Diablo today, at once leveraging their credits for marketing (they're about to launch a Kickstarter) and resisting the idea that they are making an unofficial Diablo sequel. I don't get the sense that any of them outright despise Diablo IV - summarised by Alice Bell as "2023's prettiest RSI machine" - but Shenk in particular argues that the game has squandered “the magic” of previous games by focussing on smooth progression and balancing and in general, “overly engineering the experience” in order to keep people glued to the game’s live service.

entry.title: Pathologic 3 is the rare game about healing that knows healing can be cruel
entry.summary:
Videogames have given us many fascinating healing mechanics and ideas about healing, from the motley support playstyles of Overwatch to the musical cooldown management of Wild Growth, but one thing developers rarely capture is that healing is an expression of power over somebody. However kind, it has the potential to be demeaning, intrusive, even abusive. In my experience of doctors and hospitals, healing is a competition between interpretations of sickness and injury, where the doctor has at their disposal all the crushing cultural authority and ornate vocabularies of modern medicine. The patient’s own self-knowledge - amassed over years of living in and with their own flesh - risks being recast as 'amateurish'. And this is before we get into the weeds of different conceptions of bodies and how they relate, which a doctor - especially an overworked, desensitised one, fighting a wider crisis - might be inclined to dismiss as mysticism or superstition.

entry.title: Adviser of EU’s Highest Court Backs VPN Neutrality in Anne Frank Copyright Battle
entry.summary: A landmark copyright battle involving digital copies of the iconic Anne Frank diary is helping to answer key questions about geo-blocking and a copyright enforcement tool. According to a new opinion from EU Advocate General Rantos, publishers who use 'state-of-the-art' blocks are not liable for copyright infringement, even if users bypass them with a VPN. Crucially, the opinion also shields VPN providers, labeling them neutral intermediaries who aren't responsible for their users' digital trespassing.
